corpusSummary: This 2026 corpus assembles social-science studies on large language models (LLMs) that examine trust, embodiment, governance, and social impact, while positioning AI as both a research instrument and a mediator of education, health, policy, and culture. It highlights methodological innovations, equity considerations, and the persistent limits of AI in situated knowledge, urging validation, transparency, and careful interpretation.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction and social dynamics
themes.description: Explores how humans perceive and interact with AI, including trust, anthropomorphism, embodied attitudes, and the emergence of polarization and social capital effects in AI-mediated contexts.

themes.name: AI as methodological tool and governance
themes.description: Proposes LLM-based workflows, evaluation frameworks, and governance models to enable rigorous, transparent, and ethical AI-enabled research across disciplines.

themes.name: AI in education, health literacy, and well-being
themes.description: Summarizes AI's roles in learning, tutoring, assessment, health information, misinformation, and broader well-being, with attention to literacy, accessibility, and equity.

themes.name: Culture, embodiment, and ethics of AI outputs
themes.description: Addresses culture and ethics in AI outputs, including embodiment gaps, synthetic spirituality, representation biases, and AI's interactions with religious, heritage, and gendered content.
